newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet crash could have been avoided-U.S. agency.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet crash could have been avoided-U.S. agency.

text.p: Federal investigators said Tuesday that ValuJet Flight 592, which crashed last year killing 110 people on board, probably would not have crashed if the plane had been fitted with a fire suppression and warning system.

At an all-day hearing on the flight's May 11, 1996, plunge into the Florida Everglades, the National Transportation Safety Board also said regulators, Valujet executives and the airline's maintenance contractor share the blame for the accident.

"The ValuJet accident resulted from failures all up and down the line -- from federal regulators to airline executives in the boardroom to workers on the shop room floor," National Transportation Safety Board Chairman Jim Hall said at the conclusion of an all-day hearing on the crash.

The NTSB confirmed the crash was caused by a fire in the cargo hold fueled by oxygen-generating canisters that had been improperly handled and labeled by SabreTech Corp., the outside maintenance contractor for ValuJet Airlines Inc.

ValuJet's failure to oversee its contract maintenance program was also cited as a factor. The NTSB also pinned blame on the Federal Aviation Administration, which failed to carry out a 1988 NTSB recommendation to require airlines to install smoke alarms and fire suppression systems in cargo holds.
